source: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
description: Echinocactus or Barrel Cactus is a small genus of cacti that includes 5 accepted species that are indigenous to the Southwestern United States and Mexico. In the past, this genus included hundreds of species, but in the 1900s, noted cactus taxonomists, Nathaniel Britton and Joseph Rose, moved most species into different genera. The famous golden barrel cactus is now correctly called Kroenleinia grusonii . The genus name, Echinocactus , originates from the Greek words echinos , meaning "hedgehog," and kaktos , meaning "thistle." This genus is known for its rounded, ball-like shape that may elongate with age. It is a member of the cactus family (Cactaceae). These plants grow best in full sun, but they can tolerate a little bit of shade. They prefer low humidity, dry soil, and need a cactus mix with coarse sand or perlite to promote good drainage. The species in this genus have robust spines and yellow or pink funnel-shaped flowers. The fruits vary from dry and wooly to fleshy and round. Many cultivars exist with unusual knobby or fasciated growth, and all have many spines. They vary greatly in size and are much smaller when grown in a pot. The plant can be easily grown as a houseplant in a container, and it is tolerant to a wide array of conditions. Quick ID: Ball-like or barrel-like shape Clearly defined rows of vertical ribs with long, sharp spines Wool-like fuzz at the top of the stem where the flowers emerge Funnel-shaped flowers with numerous petals Insects, Diseases, and Other Plant Problems: . May be susceptible to aphids, mealybugs, scale, and whiteflies. Overwatering can cause root rot. cultivars.name: Echinocactus horizonthalonius (Turk's Head Cactus)
cultivars.note: small barrel cactus, unbranched, pale grayish-green to grayish-blue, pinkish-red flowers

cultivars.name: Echinocactus parryi
cultivars.note: dense, upright, multi-colored spines that may be in shades of cream, pink to red with purple hues

cultivars.name: Echinocactus platyacanthus (Visnaga)
cultivars.note: solitary, largest of the barrel cacti, stem grayish-blue, yellow flowers

cultivars.name: Echinocactus polycephalus
cultivars.note: dense, spiny cactus, forms 20 to 30 heads, 2 feet tall, 4 feet wide, spines with white hairs

cultivars.name: Echinocactus texensis (Horse Crippler Cactus)
cultivars.note: broader than long, 1 to 2 inches tall, 12 inches wide, difficult to see, many horses have been crippled by the plant

cultivars.name: Echinocactus x diabolicus (E. horizonthalonius x E. platycanthus)
cultivars.note: hybrid, bluish green stem, white and fluffy areoles, long yellowish-brown spines

Distribution: Mexico, Arizona, California, Nevada, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas, and Utah.
Light: Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day)
Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)
Fruit Description: The fruits may be dry and wooly or fleshy and round.
Flower Description: Flowers emerge from the top of the plant, the buds forming a ring. The brightly colored flowers of yellow or pink are usually funnel-shaped with numerous petals.
Leaf Description: This plant has spines, which are modified leaves, that are long and recurved. They can be densely packed.
Stem Description: The apex may grow a wool-like fiber, creating a ring where the flowers emerge.
